Latin word

necessitūdō

necessitūdō, necessitūdinis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a close bond, close friendship or kinship; a close tie, a relationship (of family, friendship or duty)

In this lexicon

  • be on good terms with

    also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.176: nūlla tibi cum istō cognātiō, nūlla necessitūdō (Lewis & Short s.v. cognātiō); Traupman 109: mihi cum (+ abl.) magna necessitūdō est

  • relationship

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.27.2: summā necessitūdine et summā conjūnctiōne adductus; Cic. Sest. 39: sunt mihi cum illō omnēs amīcitiae necessitūdinēs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • et hercule multā et jūcundā cōnsuētūdine conjūnctī inter nōs sumus

    and, I tell you, we are joined by a close and pleasant relationshipCic. Att. 1.16.11

    In the entry for relationship

  • in omnibus novīs conjūnctiōnibus interest quālis prīmus aditus sit

    in every new relationship a great deal depends on how the first approach is madeCic. Fam. 13.10.4

    In the entry for relationship

  • etsī amor mē graviter cōnsuētūdōque ejus tenet

    though love and my relationship with her still hold me fastTer. Hec. 404

    In the entry for relationship

  • cōnsuētūdinem cum aliquō habēre

    to have an affair with someoneTraupman 269
